solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: How things went for winners at pool?

definitions.text: How things went for winners at pool?

parts.words: How things went for winners at pool?
parts.note: the winners of a race at the swimming pool did well in the water, and the word for that also means things went very smoothly

explanation.surface: A question about how the day went for the victors at a swimming gala.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is an idiom for very smoothly and successfully, used of how events went.

clue.text: Welsh are surrounding hospital — other ranks to come from south with valiant soldier

indicators.note: the word are goes round the hospital letter, holding it inside

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming from the south means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A Welsh unit around a field hospital, with the rank and file arriving from the south to join a brave soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts the hospital letter inside the word are; 'to come from south' means the other-ranks letters are read upward, as this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier honoured for courage in combat is called by this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Mother Goose at first seen by American priest

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Goose is taken

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme figure Mother Goose being spotted by an American clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen by' is a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus was a priest of ancient Persia, the singular of the Magi of the Nativity story.

clue.text: Who cause things to burn bright in frolicking with tigers?

definitions.text: Who cause things to burn bright

indicators.note: frolicking suggests lively, disordered movement, so the letters of in and tigers are scrambled

explanation.surface: A question about who makes things blaze while romping with big cats, a Blake-like burning tiger image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolicking' rearranges IN plus TIGERS; the surface echoes Blake's 'Tyger, tyger, burning bright'.
explanation.definitionFit: People or devices that set things alight and make them burn are, by agent noun, those that ignite.

clue.text: Does it surround country house in Kent perhaps?

definitions.text: Does it surround country house in Kent perhaps?

parts.words: Does it surround country house in Kent perhaps?
parts.note: a garden surrounds a country house, and the county of Kent has a famous nickname calling it the orchard-rich garden of the whole nation

explanation.surface: A question about the grounds around a stately home in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent, a county in south-east England known for orchards and hop fields, has long been nicknamed with this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional nickname for Kent, praising its fruit-growing and hop-farming countryside.

clue.text: God has cut and dried grass sent towards heaven

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending letters skyward means reading them from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: to hew is to cut, as with an axe
hay is grass that has been cut and dried for fodder

explanation.surface: A deity with mown and dried grass offered up to the skies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent towards heaven' turns the whole run HEWHAY upward, giving the letters backwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Hebrew name for the God of Israel in the Old Testament.

clue.text: English study delightful place

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat room

explanation.surface: An English study described as a lovely spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden is used by extension for any paradise or place of delight.

clue.text: Throwing pie is rude old playwright

indicators.note: throwing suggests tossing things about, so the letters of pie is rude are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that hurling custard pies is bad manners.
explanation.definitionFit: He was one of the three great tragic dramatists of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Look of cricket side having peculiarly neat attire?

definitions.text: Look of cricket side having peculiarly neat attire?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are taken to hold the cricket side inside them, as something has a thing within
peculiarly signals the letters of neat are arranged oddly

parts.note: leg is the on side of the cricket field, behind a right-handed batsman's legs

explanation.surface: Admiring a cricket team turned out in unusually smart whites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiarly' scrambles the word neat and 'having' holds the cricket side inside it; the whole clue also defines, since a neatly dressed team looks smart. The leg side is one half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: A team in neat attire looks smart and stylish, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Boast of rupees in sack

indicators.note: in places the rupees letter within the word for a sack

parts.note: a bag is a sack
R is the abbreviation for rupees, the Indian currency

explanation.surface: Showing off about the rupees stuffed in a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast is to talk proudly about oneself, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Enthrone with two kings fighting for Yorkshireman?

indicators.note: fighting suggests a scuffle, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: R, from rex, is the abbreviation for king, so two kings give two Rs

explanation.surface: Two rival kings battling over who gets crowned, as in a Wars of the Roses scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting' rearranges ENTHRONE plus RR. Yorkshire is a county in the north of England, hence the question mark: a Yorkshireman is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkshireman is an example of someone from the north of England.

clue.text: Wealthy hedonists' pet rhymes

parts.note: two words that rhyme with pet supply the first half of the phrase
a second word rhyming with pet supplies the other half

explanation.surface: The favourite verses of the idle rich.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves of the answer rhyme with 'pet'; the possessive on 'hedonists' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names rich, fashionable people who fly around the world for pleasure.

clue.text: Former knight seen timelessly as model

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: without time means the letter standing for time is removed

parts.note: a Templar was a knight of the medieval crusading order

explanation.surface: A one-time knight regarded as a role model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timelessly' takes T (time) out of TEMPLAR, leaving EMPLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a model or perfect example to be copied.

clue.text: Who chases female spy after time in wee room?

indicators.note: in places the time-and-spy pieces within the word for a small room

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet, a room for a wee

indicators.note: after says the spy comes behind the time letter

parts.note: Mata Hari was the famous dancer and spy of the First World War

explanation.surface: A secret agent tailing a woman into the toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British for toilet, and 'wee' is both small and urination.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, named after a rake in an 18th-century play.

clue.text: As a broomstick may be misused by women

definitions.meaning: a witch's broomstick may be ridden by a hag
the word also means tormented or harassed, as if by witches

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means tormented or harassed, literally ridden by a witch.

clue.text: Lover's meeting in tree

definitions.meaning: a palm that bears sweet brown fruit

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a romantic outing and the fruit-bearing palm.

clue.text: Restrict dangerous driver — one often flat out on road?

definitions.text: one often flat out on road?

parts.note: to hedge is to restrict or hem in
a road hog is a selfish, reckless driver

explanation.surface: Curbing a reckless motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat out' looks like full speed but means lying squashed: a hedgehog is often roadkill.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedgehogs are notoriously run over, so one is often found flattened on the road.

clue.text: He composed letter after a bit of work

parts.note: the letter that follows A in the alphabet
an erg is a tiny unit of work or energy in physics

explanation.surface: A composer writing a letter after a spell of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a' is read literally: the letter after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Magical place to see African beast drinking fluid

indicators.note: the beast drinking takes the fluid into itself

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope
FL is an abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz

explanation.surface: A trip to watch an African antelope at a waterhole.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfland is the fairy realm of elves, a place of magic.

clue.text: Anything but odd number for prayer service

parts.note: the opposite of odd is even
a number is a song or piece in a performance

explanation.surface: A count that is anything but odd, for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a figure, but it is a musical number.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service of the Anglican Church.

clue.text: Falls head over heels once more with artist

indicators.note: turning head over heels flips the word upside down, so backwards in this down light

parts.note: again means once more
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Someone falling head over heels in love again with a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head over heels' turns AGAIN into NIAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Fourth version sent up to Indian man?

indicators.note: in a down entry, sent up means the letters read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a fourth model is called Mark IV, with Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A fourth edition being sent to an Indian man.
explanation.definitionFit: Vikram is a common male given name in India, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Joining together very good fellow with another nine in gay capital

parts.note: A, as in A-class or top grade, means very good
F is the abbreviation for fellow, and another one makes two
IX is nine in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Uniting a fine chap with another nine in a party city.
explanation.definitionFit: Affixing means attaching or fastening one thing to another.

clue.text: International blog rewritten by top-grade student

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters of blog are set down again in a new order

parts.note: A is the top grade in exams
L, for learner, stands for a student, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An international blog being redrafted by a star student.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means worldwide, a synonym for international.

clue.text: Disc unaltered for Manchester band

parts.note: a disc is round, like the letter O
as is means unaltered, in its current state

explanation.surface: A record left untouched by a Manchester group.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis was the famous rock band from Manchester, led by the Gallagher brothers.

clue.text: Norse god — that's nonsense!

parts.note: Balder is the Norse god of light, son of Odin
the punctuation mark in the clue is a dash

explanation.surface: Dismissing a Norse god as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed dash is a piece of the wordplay, not punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash means senseless talk or rubbish, a synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Look in small container

parts.note: a can is a container

explanation.surface: Peering into a little tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over something carefully.

clue.text: God takes overdose at home

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A deity taking an overdose at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Absurd vehicle powered by green source in the country

parts.note: mad means absurd
a car running on gas, taken as a clean fuel, is a gas car

explanation.surface: A silly eco-friendly car somewhere out in rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like countryside, but it is a nation, the island off East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is an island country in the Indian Ocean off East Africa.
